subject: atomic-agent
title: Claims need evidence: a final reply reporting a check ('tests pass', 'verified', 'ran node --check on all files') is matched against the turn's actual tool calls; a claim with none holds the reply back with one notice and one more step, the second claim ships but is trace-marked
one_why: Closes the model-lies-about-having-checked hole with pure arithmetic over the turn transcript (no judge, no model call); warn-once keeps it from nagging, and the doc comment names the three real sessions that motivated it - strongest occupant alongside octomind's gate.rs for this concept.

subject: atomic-agent
title: GBNF grammar-constrained tool calls for local models: array-only root kills first-token bias into single-object form, per-request grammar narrowing (tool-name set rewritten, every other byte identical, cached by sorted list) travels outside the KV-cached prefix, and a bounded think-body rule (think-char{0,N}) forces runaway reasoners to close the block and emit the call
evidence: grammars/tool-call.gbnf; src/llm/grammar/build-grammar.ts; src/llm/grammar/reasoning-prelude.ts; AGENTS.md:22 (invariant 4, F49); src/llm/grammar/build-grammar.test.ts
one_why: The corpus's only local-model-native decode guard: degenerate whitespace loops and 22-minute thinking spirals are made unrepresentable at the sampler level rather than detected post-hoc, and narrowing the allowed tool set mid-session costs zero cache re-prefill because the grammar never enters the cached prefix.

subject: atomic-agent
title: KV-cache-monotonic prompt architecture: stable prefix pinned byte-identical per session (tests assert byte-equality), everything a step can change placed AFTER ### conversation in the variable tail, per-request grammar kept out of the prefix, conversation pack holds a 0.65 low-water hysteresis, and cache hits are measured server-side (cacheHitTokens) and surfaced per step in traces
one_why: Cache discipline expressed as prompt LAYOUT + hysteresis instead of fold economics - the ordering rule ('a change lands behind the transcript the model already read') is portable to API providers as cache-breakpoint placement, and the measured-hit feedback closes the loop the jazz/g3 rows only estimate.

subject: atomic-agent
title: Approval grant-scope correctness bundle: grant scope names come from the caller but category/shape are read from the gate's OWN pending request (a host cannot grant a category the prompt was not about), shape grants use the guard-normalized argv[0] and are withheld for opaque interpreters (bash -c), trust_config is never session-grantable, and fs-read-outside is pinned so only full trust runs wandering reads unasked
one_why: The corpus's cleanest positive pole for approval-scope correctness (against neovate's category-cache amnesia): value-vs-scope separation at the gate boundary plus opaque-interpreter withholding makes 'approve git' mean exactly approve-git; realpath containment also avoids mini-kode's sibling-prefix grant. Roadmap-fit: copy the gate-owns-the-value rule.

subject: atomic-agent
title: Fan-out delegation earns a scoped grant: one operator approval lets fusion workers write and run commands inside one named directory for exactly one turn - grants cleared at turn START so an aborted turn cannot leave authority behind, scoped command runs stay cwd-bounded ('the directory is the whole of the promise'), and the orchestrator's never-mutate gate had two documented escape hatches closed at their source
one_why: Turn-scoped, directory-bounded, single-purpose delegation authority - the strongest subagent-permission model in the corpus (contrast codemachine's bypass-launching); the module doc's post-mortems (latch-on-attempt, needs_orchestrator hatch) are a free audit checklist for hotdog's own subagent grants. New id; sibling to subagent-process-delegation but the axis is grant scope, not process model.

subject: atomic-agent
title: Context window learned from provider refusals: a 400/413 naming the real window repacks the next prompt to it once (or estimates 0.8x the refused prompt when no number is named, with a 1024-token plausibility floor), then corrects the model catalog via onContextWindowObserved - a mid-session model swap re-probes before step 0
one_why: Measured-not-assumed window truth: the catalog starts as a guess (128k default) and the provider's own error text is the calibration source; the 'already retried once' bound prevents shrink-loops. New id, usage-measured family sibling (usage-measured-compact-trigger x10).

subject: atomic-agent
title: Semantic loop layers above byte-repeat: test-repeat detector warns on the 2nd equivalent test command against an UNCHANGED workspace fingerprint (a rerun cannot produce new evidence), read-coverage detector flags redundant re-reads, batched steps hash as one composite entry so identical batches trip but permuted ones don't, and warnings bucket-dedup so the notice isn't re-injected every step
one_why: Meaning-aware breakers (semantic test key + workspace fingerprint + coverage) rather than call-hash repetition - crush's seeded loop-detection rung plus two semantic axes; the permuted-batch tolerance is the right false-positive posture.

subject: atomic-agent
title: Corpus-class eval harness wired to zero CI: GAIA-style agent evals, LoCoMo, LongMemEval, 12 memory-campaign experiments and competitor adapters all exist, and eval/vitest.config.ts explicitly states they must never run under npm test - but the only workflows are test.yml and release.yml
evidence: .github/workflows/ (2 files); eval/vitest.config.ts:4-8; eval-agents/scripts/run-matrix.mjs; eval-memory/scripts/run-all.mjs; package.json eval:* scripts
one_why: Fourth instance of instrumented-but-unenforced (deepagents/forge/jazz): keeps verification pinned at the ERRATA 8-ceiling for a subject whose eval investment is arguably the corpus's largest - the cheapest 9-claim wire-up in the study.

subject: atomic-agent
title: Two red tests excluded from the CI vitest run to keep main green (send-message-concurrency, local-models-orchestrator-auto-update) - loudly documented with root causes and tracked in issue #203, but they are real tests silently absent from the gate
one_why: Ruled trivia per the amazon-q broken-CI precedent (loud, narrow 2/931, issue-tracked - not silently-skipped-at-scale, not red-and-ignored); filed for the record as a kimi-code-b1 sibling: tests visible, gate blind. No lane dock.

subject: atomic-agent
title: Six-way rival harness migration: first run offers to bring skills, memory, MCP servers, sessions, cron jobs and (opt-in) provider keys over from Hermes, OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, Pi and Oh-My-Pi with a dry-run preview before anything is written
evidence: src/import/claude-code/; src/import/codex/; src/import/pi/pi-session-format.ts; src/import/hermes/; src/import/oh-my-pi/; src/import/openclaw/; src/import/detect-import-agents.ts; src/import/reconcile-session.ts
one_why: Adversarial-interoperability as a growth surface: the switching cost away from rivals is deleted while rival adapters (codemachine-style) only run rivals with safety off - interop credit that HIDES no safety sub-floor, the cross-check gemini-cli/kilocode synthesis asked for.

subject: atomic-agent
title: Honest pole of subscription transport: the operator's own logged-in official claude/codex CLIs are spawned as LLM providers (spawn('claude'), /login auth hints, rate-limit mapping) - no prompt-level identity spoofing, no wire emulation
one_why: Third occupant of the cluster (grinta rival-subscription-transport, qqcode vendor-protocol-impersonation): atomic rides the vendor CLI exactly as its EULA-shaped interface intends, which gives synthesis a contrast case for where ToS-risk kinks (transport via official CLI vs impersonation at the wire).

subject: atomic-agent
title: Memory fabric with its own eval program: reflection fires on turn segmentation, a consolidator job merges notes, lessons/procedures are pointer-indexed sections outside the cache prefix, the profile store is bitemporal, and each phase shipped with named eval campaigns (E1-E12, LoCoMo, LongMemEval, competitor baselines)
one_why: Memory subsystems are common; memory subsystems with per-phase falsifiable hypotheses and competitor baselines are not - the agent-loop.ts:1137-1159 comment even documents a caught bug where reflection writes silently landed 0-for-75-turns. Claims of memory QUALITY unverified here (evals not run in CI), hence med confidence.
